rules.sentence: Diagnosis is challenging and often delayed due to its nonspecific presentation.

Abdominal TB responds well to standard antituberculous drugs when diagnosed early, with surgery only required in cases that develop complications (eg, strictures or obstruction) or that are unresponsive to medical therapy.
High clinical suspicion, early initiation of antituberculous therapy, and involvement of an interprofessional team are necessary for reducing morbidity and mortality.
High clinical suspicion and early antituberculous therapy are essential for favorable outcomes, although surgery may be required for complications like obstruction, perforation, or strictures.
